A denial statement (Deny) in the policy of the bucket with the condition 'StringNotEquals' in the header 's3:x-amz-server-side-encryption' rejects, at the level of API, any 'PutObject' which does not specify the required encryption — this denial applies to QUALQUER main (since the main of the declaration is '*'), regardless of your permissions IAM the individual, taking into account the 'requirement regardless of which main'.

Incorrect. Default encryption automatically encrypts objects that do NOT specify configurations of SSE, but no REJEITA uploads — it does not require a specific header to be present, and a different type of encryption explicitly specified by the sender could still be ACEITO (overlapping the default), failing to reject non-compliant uploads.

Incorrect. Attach the same condition to the policy of the IAM of CADA main individually is operationally fragile (need to be replicated to any current and future main, including main accounts of other accounts over which the team may not have control) — a single statement in the bucket policy applies the requirement centrally, regardless of the main, which is much more robust.

Incorrect. S3 Object Lock controls retention behavior WORM (write-once-read-many) to prevent the deletion/modification of objects (retention/legal hold) — is not related to requiring a specific encryption configuration on the server's side in PutObject requests.

Which configuration achieves this goal?
options: Define the identity source of the Lambda Authorize as 'context.requestId', so that each request is treated as unique and stored in cache independently.

Configure the Lambda Authorizer with 'authorizerResultTtlInSeconds' defined as 300 (5 minutes) and 'identitysource' defined as the heading 'Authorization' — the API Gateway will cache the policy IAM returned by the author, indexed by the value of 'identitySource' (the key to API in the heading 'Authorization', by TTL configured; subsequent requests with the MESMO header value inside the window of TTL re-use cache policy SEM invoke the Lambda Authorizer.
Increase the assigned memory of the function Lambda Authorizer to speed up the consultation DynamoDB, reducing additional latency by requisitioning.
Enable response cache (cache cluster) at method level in API Gateway for protected methods, with a TTL of 300 seconds.
dva-avc-084.explanation: Correct. 'authorizerResultTtlInSeconds' controls for how long API Gateway caches the result (policy document IAM) returned by Lambda Authorizer, using the value of 'identitySource' (here, the header 'Authorization' containing the key to API) as a cache key. Requirements with the same cache key API within TTL re-use the cached result, avoiding the invocation of the authorizer and the query to the DynamoDB.
